claims.text: Moneytrail processes bank statements locally, ensuring that data never exits the user's machine.
The tool validates data by checking the running balance column and verifying that opening balance plus credits minus debits equals the closing balance.
The software avoids floating-point math, treating all monetary values as integer counts of paise to maintain precision.
The project includes 499 tests and maintains a passing status on Python versions 3.11 and 3.12.
Credit card statements are verified using a summary box calculation and by ensuring the sum of recovered transaction rows matches the stated totals.
Scanned PDF files are intentionally rejected by the software rather than being processed with guesswork.
The software successfully reconciled 225 transactions from an HDFC bank statement over a three-month period against the bank's own summary balance.
Initial testing with real-world data identified four specific formatting issues that synthetic test data failed to capture.
The system uses minimum-cost segmentation over a vocabulary to separate combined merchant names.
Only 18% of the transactions in the tested statement were identified as recognized merchants.
The majority of transactions in the analyzed ledger consisted of person-to-person transfers (41%), credit-card bill repayments (18%), and bank charges or interest (5%).
Counting both the bank debit for a card payment and the corresponding reduction in the credit card balance results in double-counting the same expenditure.
Card repayments lacking a corresponding card statement are still included in spending totals to avoid the risk of understating expenses.
The software identifies recurring charges by measuring actual cadence rather than assuming a subscription based on transaction frequency.
Transfers between a user's own accounts are matched and removed from both inflow and outflow reports to prevent artificial inflation of spending and income figures.
Most bank statements do not contain ruling lines, which causes many standard conversion tools to fail.
The moneytrail project previously relied on its own generated PDFs for testing, which led to a false sense of success.
The tool determines column boundaries by analyzing the geometric gaps between header names.
Bank rows often span multiple lines, requiring the software to group lines together based on the presence of a date.
The system dynamically calculates the threshold for column gaps per line, using values such as 1.8pt for word spaces and 12.7pt for column gaps on HDFC headers.
Files where the text layer lacks proper column information are rejected to prevent the creation of ledgers that reconcile against incorrect totals.
Exported files include a reconciliation certificate containing the SHA-256 hash of the source bytes and the results of arithmetic checks.
Statements that fail to reconcile are still exported, but they are marked with a reconciliation status of 'NO' and trigger a non-zero exit code.
To ensure data accuracy, amounts are written as exact decimals rather than floats, and CSV files are saved with a BOM to maintain character encoding.
The software provides a certificate, trust strip, and workbook as a single PDF file, which the browser saves directly from memory without using a download endpoint.
The application's CLI guarantees that no data leaves the local machine.
The server remains stateless because it does not store data between requests, ensuring no second request can access the uploaded information.
The web interface is a single HTML file that avoids build steps, CDNs, and analytics to ensure it contains no external references.
The demo version includes a sample file with one row of ₹649 removed to demonstrate how the tool catches missing data.
The hosted service offers a free tier for single statements, while batch processing requires a license key.
License keys function as bearer tokens stored in the user's browser, allowing the system to avoid using accounts or databases.
The payment gate is only active on the hosted instance, meaning local runs and self-hosted versions remain entirely unlocked.
To prevent service interruptions during payment processor outages, license keys are cached for one day after a successful verification.
The generated report categorizes financial data by reconciliation status, open loops, recurring payments, and spending categories.
A language model can generate a confident but incorrect total when tasked with reading a ledger directly.
The system prevents incorrect answers by requiring that every result is accompanied by the specific ledger rows used to calculate it.
The moneytrail tool correctly identifies when a requested merchant does not exist in the provided statements rather than returning an incorrect aggregate.
Relative date queries like 'last month' are resolved against the ledger's timeline to ensure consistent answers over time.
The system explicitly informs users when a requested transaction, such as a refund, cannot be found in the ledger.
The project uses a scorecard of 71 questions to evaluate performance, with 40 percent of the questions held back from the model to prevent overfitting.
The system supports multiple LLM providers including Groq, OpenAI, Gemini, Together, OpenRouter, and Ollama through a single environment variable configuration.
The built-in regex parser achieves 65.5% query accuracy and 55.2% answer accuracy.
The openai/gpt-oss-120b model reaches 89.7% query accuracy and 93.1% answer accuracy at a cost of $0.000291 per question.
The openai/gpt-oss-20b model achieves 89.7% query accuracy and 93.1% answer accuracy at a cost of $0.000151 per question.
The llama-3.3-70b-versatile model reaches 89.7% query accuracy and 93.1% answer accuracy at a cost of $0.000657 per question.
The llama-3.1-8b-instant model achieves 69.0% query accuracy and 79.3% answer accuracy at a cost of $0.000056 per question.
The built-in regex parser scores 0% on questions that require model-only capabilities.

The openai/gpt-oss-20b model is identified as the most efficient choice because it provides identical accuracy to larger models at a quarter of the price of the 70B model while offering the fastest p50 speed.
Prompt tuning against a visible development set can lead to performance degradation on held-out data due to rule conflicts.
Some user questions, such as comparing months or identifying subscription price changes, are fundamentally inexpressible within the current query schema.
